best_for: Windows developers who must build or patch a project still pinned to .NET 9, and who plan to move it to .NET 10 soon.
description:
.NET is a free, open-source app platform backed by Microsoft. It sits under the .NET Foundation, an independent organization that supports open development around it. The SDK is the kit you install to write and build .NET apps, not just run them.

With it you can build web apps and services, microservices that run in Docker containers, 2D and 3D games, and apps for single-board computers like the Raspberry Pi. NuGet, the package manager, holds more than 300,000 packages to pull into a project. Work from the .NET command line, Visual Studio or Visual Studio Code, and set up automatic builds on services such as GitHub Actions.

points.title: Support ended on November 10, 2026
points.text: .NET 9 was a Standard Term Support release, which gets two years of fixes. Microsoft ended support on November 10, 2026 and now lists it as out of support. New projects are better started on .NET 10, the current Long Term Support release, which runs to November 14, 2028.

points.title: Two SDK lines, one runtime
points.text: The 9.0 SDK shipped in two feature bands, 9.0.1xx and 9.0.3xx. Both carry the same 9.0 runtime patches. The 3xx line pairs with Visual Studio 2022 version 17.14 and the 1xx line with 17.12, so pick the band your Visual Studio expects.

points.title: Three runtimes in the box
points.text: SDK 9.0.321 brings the .NET Runtime, the ASP.NET Core Runtime and the .NET Desktop Runtime, all at 9.0.23. It compiles C# 13, F# 9 and Visual Basic 17.13, so one install covers console, web and Windows desktop apps.

points.title: Telemetry is on by default
points.text: CLI commands such as `dotnet build` send usage data to Microsoft, and the installer sends one entry after a good install. Set the `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT` environment variable to `1` before you install to turn both off. Running a built app with `dotnet app.dll` sends nothing.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: The SDK costs nothing and is released under the MIT license. No account or sign-in is needed to install it or build with it.

points.title: Windows only on this page
points.text: This listing has x64, x86 and Arm64 installers for Windows, all installing for every user on the machine, and keeps 53 versions. Microsoft also publishes macOS installers and Linux archives on its own download page.
